Three directions, four views. Pick where to commit.

Each cell below shows a Honeycomb mockup (clickable for the polished Blend variants, in-line wireframe for the other views) side-by-side with the actual Mobbin screens it draws from. The three directions are Cream Editorial (pair-friendly knowledge register), Hex + Editorial (brand-defining triad, the literal honeycomb metaphor), and Dark Constellation (peer-celestial triad, the most ambitious).

Click any Mobbin thumbnail to open it on Mobbin. The Blend mockups (top section) are real interactive prototypes — open A, B, and C in new tabs to compare in motion. Background research in 01-mood-board, 02-pattern-extraction, 04-anti-patterns.

View 1 of 4

Blend

The load-bearing decision. Pair Blend (2-way overlap) and triad Blend (1 three-way + 3 pairwise zones) need a visualization that's legible without becoming a math diagram. This is where directions diverge most.

Direction A · Cream Editorial

Pair as co-authored chapbook

Editorial serif, warm cream, oversized italic headlines. Two-name lockup over translucent overlapping circles, themes as emoji-prefixed pills, per-person quote attribution under each shared theme. The safest, most knowledge-shaped register.

Direction C · Dark Constellation

Themes as stars in a peer field

Continuous 2-D gravitational field on dark navy. Three glowing peer orbs at triangle vertices; themes as stars positioned by who contributed. Center cluster = all three. Edges = pairwise. Near each orb = solo. The most ambitious direction.

Vault review

The agent surfaces private vault items; the user approves them per-recipient before they enter the blend. The hard problem: in triad mode, each item has at least two independent decisions (visible to Yedu? to Humzah?).

Direction A · Cream Editorial

Editorial review queue

Each agent-surfaced item is rendered as a quiet cream card with the surfaced quote in serif italic. The agent's reasoning collapses under a hairline. Below: a per-recipient pill row (one pill each for Yedu, Humzah) to toggle visibility before approving.

Shared shelf

A co-owned bookshelf-style object for the blend — saved recommendations from each member with reactions, comments, and contributor attribution. Two/three-name shelf identity, per-item contributor avatar, reactions as emoji pills.

Conversations

Prompt cards (1:1 and group-context), AI-drafted message preview, log of past in-person talks. Pair-friendly patterns dominate the field (Paired, stoic.) — Honeycomb's challenge is the *group* prompt: same question, three answer tracks.

Direction A · Cream Editorial

Magazine prompt + dated journal

Prompts render as oversized serif questions on a cream card; below the question, each member's answer appears as a dated journal entry with attribution. Past talks log inline as Clay-style dotted-divider notes.

Direction C · Dark Constellation

Prompts as inviting void

The question appears centered in the dark field; each member's answer floats nearby as a luminous card tinted in their color. Past prompts archive into a star-cluster index — each cluster a former question, each star a member's answer.

What not to copy, regardless of direction

The Mobbin sweep also surfaced patterns that would silently destabilize Honeycomb. Drop these even if they look great in the reference apps:

  • Match percentages, compatibility scores, leaderboards — the "92% compatible" trap. Honeycomb's result is a conversation, not a score.
  • "VS" framing, head-to-head bars, split-screen diff — pair-coded duality that breaks at N=3.
  • Host / owner / admin badges on any triad member — Shawn, Yedu, and Humzah are equal participants.
  • Any default ordering of members (numbered slots, alphabetical, join-date). Randomize per session or arrange radially.
  • Pairwise zones treated as "leftover" or hidden behind a More tap. Four zones, all first-class.
  • Read receipts, view counts, "seen by" — surveillance disguised as social proof.
